# [TASK] ai-service: natural-language query parsing endpoint

## Task
Add a new ai-service endpoint that turns a raw natural-language query into a
structured filter (or a plain-title fallback) using Ollama.

## Scope
Endpoint only — this Task does not call actor-service/movie-service or
execute the filter (that's #203). Covers the extraction contract and its
own tests only.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `POST /api/v1/ai/search/query` accepts free text, runs it through `PromptSanitizer` before it reaches the prompt — verified by a test that captures the actual `Prompt` sent to the model and checks the sanitized text, not just the HTTP response
- [x] Returns a structured filter matching ADR-020's shape, or an explicit plain-title fallback when no operators/entities are detected
- [x] Negation ("didn't direct", "not starring") is extracted as a distinct field, not silently dropped or treated as a positive match
- [x] Tests cover: multi-constraint query, plain-title query, ambiguous/unparseable query, negation — plus blank-input validation, prompt sanitization, length-cap truncation, and a partial-model-response null-safety case found in review
- [x] Javadoc on the controller method and service class (and DTOs, enum, private helpers, and every test method)

## Estimate
**Hours:** 8

## Notes
Implemented `QueryParsingService`, `StructuredQueryFilterDto`/`QueryFilterRole`/`QueryParseRequestDto`, and `POST /api/v1/ai/search/query`, following `RecommendationService`'s sanitize-then-prompt pattern. Not user-scoped — parsing touches no per-user data.

`StructuredQueryFilterDto` has a canonical constructor defaulting `collaborators`/`negated` to empty lists, since Jackson leaves an omitted record component null rather than failing.

Known limitation, documented in `QueryParsingService#parse`: the endpoint can't yet distinguish "the model found no structure" from "extraction failed" — both return 200. Fixing it would need an ADR-020 amendment, since the contract shape is pinned there.
